name: Claude Code
official_status_notes: Anthropic's agentic coding tool: CLI, VS Code/JetBrains extensions, desktop app, web; MCP; Agent SDK (verified docs Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Requires Claude Pro/Max subscription or API/Bedrock/Vertex; third-party OAuth providers supported.
best_for: Terminal-first workflows, long-running agent sessions, and deep repo understanding.
strengths: Mature CLI agent, subagents, hooks, CLAUDE.md memory, MCP, IDE extensions, scripting/headless modes.
weaknesses: Anthropic-centric billing; subscription needed for the smoothest experience.
hardware_requirements: Any machine; runs in terminal (Windows w/ PowerShell/WSL).

name: OpenAI Codex CLI
official_status_notes: Open-source CLI (Apache-2.0) for the Codex coding agent; runs in terminal and IDE extension; cloud Codex runs in sandboxes (verified Sep 2026). Includes SQLite history, MCP client support.
pricing_summary: CLI is free/open source; requires OpenAI API/Advanced subscription; usage-based API cost.
best_for: Developers who want a capable, scriptable terminal agent with OpenAI models.
strengths: Open-source CLI, agentic, sandboxing, MCP, IDE extension, supports subscription auth.
weaknesses: Model choice mainly OpenAI; long autonomous runs cost API tokens.

name: Gemini CLI
official_status_notes: Open-source (Apache-2.0) terminal agent for Gemini; free personal tier, BYOK API, MCP support, extensions (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free to use for personal use via Google sign-in; BYOK for API; enterprise via Google Cloud.
best_for: Free, open-source terminal agent for Gemini models with MCP support, extensions, and a VS Code companion.
strengths: Latency, 1M context, style adaptation.
weaknesses: Autocomplete/chat only; no autonomous agent.

name: OpenCode
official_status_notes: The original sst/opencode repo was archived 2025-09-18 (its lineage continued as Crush by Charm). The OpenCode product now lives at github.com/anomalyco/opencode and is under very active development: MIT license, build/plan agents, desktop app beta (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK.
best_for: An open-source, actively developed terminal coding agent with plan/build agents, a desktop app (beta), and broad provider support.
strengths: TUI, LSP, MCP, session control, BYOK.
weaknesses: Archived; use Crush instead.

name: Aider
official_status_notes: Open-source terminal pair-programming tool; supports many cloud and local LLMs; repo map; git auto-commit; linter/test loop (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK (model API costs only).
best_for: Terminal-first editing with tight git integration and many model options.
strengths: Repo map, automatic git commits, linter/test integration, voice control, model flexibility.
weaknesses: Pair-programming (edit) focus rather than full autonomy; you drive the loop.

name: Goose
official_status_notes: Open-source (Apache-2.0) AI agent that moved to the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation) â€” vendor-neutral, community-governed; desktop app + CLI + API, 70+ MCP extensions, ACP support, BYOK across 15+ providers (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK.
best_for: Extensible, MCP-first agentic automation and local-model use.
strengths: MCP-native, extension system, local + cloud models, recipes/skills.
weaknesses: Config and extension sprawl can be finicky; younger than Claude Code/Aider.

name: OpenHands
official_status_notes: Open-source (MIT) AI-driven development platform; formerly OpenDevin; includes Agent Canvas UI + Agent Server API; cloud offering available (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, self-host; commercial cloud/enterprise options.
best_for: Autonomous, sandboxed software-engineering agents and research.
strengths: Autonomous agents, sandboxed execution, desktop app, cloud SaaS, strong research lineage.
weaknesses: Heavier to self-host; autonomy needs careful guarding.
hardware_requirements: Self-host wants a beefy machine; cloud mode is lighter.

name: Crush
official_status_notes: Open-source terminal AI agent (successor to OpenCode) from Charm; FSL-1.1-MIT license; multi-model, MCP, LSP, Windows support (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK.
best_for: Terminal-first agents with maximal model/provider flexibility.
strengths: Multi-model, mid-session model switching, MCP (http/stdio/sse), LSP awareness, cross-platform.
weaknesses: Model/provider catalog auto-updates (Catwalk) â€” watch data/config churn.

name: Pythagora
official_status_notes: GPT-Pilot lives under the Pythagora GitHub org; verify which product (GPT-Pilot vs Pythagora dev tool) is current before relying on it.
pricing_summary: GPT-Pilot is open source (MIT); Pythagora products may have paid tiers.
best_for: Understanding earlier autonomous full-app pilot agents.
strengths: Historical importance; CLI agent that builds apps stepwise.
weaknesses: Older architecture; project focus evolved.

name: SWE-agent
official_status_notes: Research project (MIT); SWE-agent 1.0 well-known. README now recommends 'mini-swe-agent' which has superseded it (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK.
best_for: Academic study of agent-computer interfaces and SWE-bench-style evaluation.
strengths: Research-grade, config-driven, evaluation tooling, EnIGMA security mode.
weaknesses: Research tool, not a polished product; mini-swe-agent recommended for new work.

name: SWE-ReX
official_status_notes: SWE-ReX is the SWE-agent team's sandboxed remote-execution runtime (MIT): massively parallel shell sessions for agents, local or cloud (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK.
best_for: Research comparison; SWE-bench style autonomous solving.
strengths: Open research implementation by BAAI.
weaknesses: Activity to verify.

name: GPT-Pilot
official_status_notes: Part of the Pythagora project family. Verify current maintenance status.
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK.
best_for: Learning about early autonomous app-piloting agents.
strengths: Historical significance; plan-based app development.
weaknesses: Older approach; maintenance uncertain â€” verify.

name: Mentat
official_status_notes: Earlier CLI editing assistant. The previously recorded repository no longer resolves (404, verified Sep 2026) â€” historical entry; verify before use.
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK.
best_for: Historical study of CLI editing agents.
strengths: Simple CLI editing approach.
weaknesses: Activity/status uncertain â€” verify.

name: Plandex
official_status_notes: Open-source (MIT) terminal AI coding agent; large projects, cumulative diff sandbox; Cloud winding down as of 2025-10-03, local/self-hosted mode recommended (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK; Plandex Cloud winding down â€” self-host recommended.
best_for: Large multi-file tasks with reviewable, rollback-able diffs.
strengths: 2M-token context, project maps, plan branches, controlled command execution, model packs.
weaknesses: Windows is WSL-only; cloud offering winding down.
hardware_requirements: Any (Go binary); self-host needs Docker for cloud mode.

name: Open Interpreter
official_status_notes: Open-source (Apache-2.0) coding agent (new Rust version based on Codex), optimized for open models like Kimi and GLM; original Python project continues via community fork (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source; model API costs if using cloud providers.
best_for: Running capable agents on open-weight/local models.
strengths: Native local model focus, sandboxing, ACP/Codex-compatible, MCP, skills.
weaknesses: Rust rewrite churn; original Python path is a community fork.
hardware_requirements: Light client; local models need RAM.

name: Warp AI
official_status_notes: Warp is an open-source terminal plus an agent platform ('factories' coordinate fleets of coding agents); Warp AI capabilities in the terminal are being retired in favor of agent platform (verified Sep 2026).
license: Apache-2.0 (terminal, open-sourced 2025); AI platform features are commercial cloud
pricing_summary: Terminal free; agent platform usage-based.
best_for: Teams automating PR review/incident workflows ('factories').
strengths: Modern terminal UX, agent platform, MCP, evals.
weaknesses: Platform pricing per-run; terminal AI features being retired.

name: Amazon Q CLI
official_status_notes: Amazon Q Developer command-line interface: autocompletions and chat for AWS CLI; part of Amazon Q Developer (verified homepage references Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Same free tier/plans as Amazon Q Developer.
best_for: AWS-centric shell workflows.
strengths: Free tier, AWS CLI completions/chat.
weaknesses: AWS-centric; limited autonomy.

name: GitHub Copilot CLI
official_status_notes: Copilot in the terminal (GitHub CLI extension and native terminal app); agentic; part of Copilot subscription (verified docs Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Part of Copilot Free/Pro/Pro+ plans.
best_for: GitHub users who want Copilot chat in the terminal.
strengths: Tight GitHub integration, agentic flows, IDE delegation.
weaknesses: Requires Copilot subscription; closed source.

name: Claude Agent SDK
official_status_notes: SDK for building agents on the Claude Code engine; enables embedding Claude Code as a library (verified docs Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: SDK is free/open; model usage billed by Anthropic.
best_for: Programmatic automation on top of the Claude Code engine.
strengths: Reuse the Claude Code engine in scripts/CI, MCP, tool registration.
weaknesses: Needs Claude API access; not a standalone end-user tool.

name: Continue CLI
official_status_notes: Open-source terminal agent from the Continue team, complementing the Continue IDE extensions. Verify current CLI commands in the official docs.
pricing_summary: Free and open source; BYOK means you pay the model provider directly; optional Continue hub features.
best_for: Developers who want one open ecosystem for both IDE and terminal agents with BYOK/local models.
strengths: Open source, BYOK + local models (Ollama), MCP support, shares configuration with Continue IDE extensions.
weaknesses: Younger terminal agent than Aider/Claude Code; fewer batteries included.
hardware_requirements: Terminal client only; model runs remote or local (local needs RAM).

name: Qwen Code
official_status_notes: Open-source (Apache-2.0) terminal coding agent, originally based on Gemini CLI v0.8.2, now independently developed; multi-protocol model access, IDE plugins (VS Code/JetBrains/Zed), desktop app, and SDK (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source; bring your own Qwen/multi-provider keys â€” verify current free-tier limits with the provider.
best_for: An open-source Claude Code-style terminal agent with Qwen and multi-provider model access.
strengths: Feature-rich (subagents, MCP, plan mode, IDE plugins); multi-protocol; open source.
weaknesses: Result quality depends on the model/plan you connect; younger than Claude Code.
hardware_requirements: Thin client; model runs in the cloud.

name: Cursor CLI
official_status_notes: Cursor's terminal agent (`agent` command): interactive and print/CI modes, Agent/Plan/Ask modes, cloud-agent handoff, resumable sessions, and sandbox controls; pairs with the Cursor IDE and subscription (verified docs Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Part of Cursor subscription plans; see the official pricing page.
best_for: Cursor subscribers who want the same agent in the terminal and CI.
strengths: Same agent/modes as the editor; print mode for scripts and CI pipelines.
weaknesses: Requires a Cursor account/subscription; closed source.
hardware_requirements: Thin client; model runs in the cloud.

name: ShellGPT
official_status_notes: MIT-licensed command-line productivity tool: generates shell commands, code snippets, and documentation from LLMs; works with an OpenAI API key or a local Ollama backend; PowerShell/CMD/Bash/Zsh; REPL and chat modes (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source; OpenAI API costs if you use cloud models.
best_for: Quick shell-command and code generation in any shell without a full coding agent.
strengths: Lightweight; Ollama support; shell-command generation with explanations.
weaknesses: Not a repo-editing agent; API costs when using cloud models.
hardware_requirements: Tiny CLI; heavy lifting happens at the model provider.

name: LLM
official_status_notes: Apache-2.0 CLI and Python library for running prompts against hosted and local models; logs prompts/responses to SQLite; plugin ecosystem; supports tools/functions (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source; provider API costs depend on the models you use.
best_for: Scriptable LLM access from the terminal with logged history â€” useful for pipelines and learning.
strengths: Model-agnostic via plugins; SQLite logging; Python library for automation.
weaknesses: Not a coding agent â€” no repo-editing loop out of the box.
hardware_requirements: Tiny CLI; heavy lifting happens at the model provider.
